MUTUAL NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT

DATED: 18 November 2026

PARTIES:

MONETAFLOW TECHNOLOGIES LTD, a company registered in England and Wales under company number 12847102, whose registered office is at 4th Floor, 80 Old Street, London EC1V 9AZ (MonetaFlow); and

HALYARD SOFTWARE LTD, a company registered in England and Wales under company number 09876543, whose registered office is at 12 Mill Lane, Manchester M1 2AB (Halyard).

MonetaFlow and Halyard may each be referred to as a "Party" or collectively as the "Parties".

BACKGROUND:
The Parties wish to explore potential collaborative and commercial opportunities in financial technology and software integration (the "Permitted Purpose"). In doing so, either Party may disclose non-public, commercially sensitive or proprietary information to the other. This Agreement establishes the ground rules to protect that information.

AGREED TERMS:

Definitions
1.1 The following definitions apply across this Agreement:
1.1.1 "Confidential Information" means all information of a confidential or proprietary nature disclosed directly or indirectly by or on behalf of one Party (the "Discloser") to the other Party (the "Recipient"), whether disclosed orally, in writing, electronically or by any other means, and whether marked as confidential or that reasonably ought to be understood as confidential given its content or the circumstances of disclosure. It includes business models, financial data, pricing, customer lists, software code, APIs, architecture, product roadmaps, algorithms and trade secrets.
1.1.2 "Representative" means a director, officer, employee, contractor, professional adviser or auditor of a Party or of any affiliate within its corporate group.

Confidentiality Obligations
2.1 In consideration of receiving Confidential Information, the Recipient agrees that it shall:
2.1.1 use Confidential Information solely to evaluate and pursue the Permitted Purpose and for no other reason;
2.1.2 hold all Confidential Information in strict confidence and apply at least the same degree of care it uses for its own confidential data of similar value, but never less than a reasonable standard of security;
2.1.3 not disclose Confidential Information to any third party, except to those of its Representatives who need to know it for the Permitted Purpose, provided such Representatives are bound by written confidentiality obligations at least as strict as those in this Agreement; and
2.1.4 be responsible for any breach of this Agreement caused by its Representatives.

Standard Carve-Outs
3.1 The obligations in Clause 2 do not apply to information that the Recipient can demonstrate:
3.1.1 is already in or enters the public domain without any breach of this Agreement;
3.1.2 was already lawfully known to the Recipient before disclosure, free of any duty of confidence;
3.1.3 is received legitimately from an independent third party who has no duty of confidentiality to the Discloser; or
3.1.4 was developed independently by the Recipient without using, referencing or relying on the Discloser's Confidential Information.

Compelled Disclosures
4.1 The Recipient may disclose Confidential Information to the extent required by an applicable law, binding court order, or formal request from a competent regulatory or supervisory authority.
4.2 Before making any disclosure under Clause 4.1, where lawful to do so, the Recipient shall promptly notify the Discloser in writing so the Discloser may seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy. The Recipient shall provide reasonable cooperation to the Discloser, at the Discloser's sole expense, in any lawful effort to resist, narrow or safeguard the disclosure.

Return and Destruction
5.1 Upon the Discloser's written request at any time, the Recipient shall promptly:
5.1.1 securely destroy or return all materials containing or reflecting Confidential Information in its custody or control; and
5.1.2 provide written confirmation that it has complied with this Clause 5.1 within ten (10) business days.
5.2 The Recipient may keep copies of Confidential Information to the extent required by applicable law, regulatory compliance or automated electronic system backups created in the ordinary course of business. Any retained copies remain subject to the obligations of this Agreement until destroyed.

Property and No Rights Granted
6.1 All Confidential Information remains the exclusive property of the Discloser.
6.2 Neither this Agreement nor any disclosure grants the Recipient any licence, title or intellectual property right in or to any Confidential Information, except the limited right to use it strictly for the Permitted Purpose.
6.3 Information is shared on an "as is" basis without warranty of any kind regarding accuracy or completeness.

Duration
7.1 This Agreement takes effect on the date set out above and remains in effect for two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party giving thirty (30) days' prior written notice.
7.2 Each Party's duty of confidentiality under this Agreement continues for three (3) years after the date of termination or expiry, except that trade secrets remain protected for as long as they constitute a trade secret under applicable law.

General
8.1 Neither Party will issue any press release or public statement mentioning the other Party or the discussions between them without prior written approval.
8.2 Each Party acknowledges that damages alone may not be an adequate remedy for breach, and each Party is entitled to seek injunctive relief and specific performance to prevent or remedy any actual or threatened breach.
8.3 Neither Party may assign or transfer its rights or obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other Party.
8.4 If any provision of this Agreement is held to be invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions will continue in full force and effect.
8.5 No failure or delay by a Party to exercise any right under this Agreement operates as a waiver of that right.
8.6 This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties relating to this subject matter and supersedes all prior discussions and understandings. Any amendment must be in writing and signed by both Parties.
8.7 This Agreement does not create any rights enforceable by any third party under the Contracts (Rights of Third Parties) Act 1999.
8.8 This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which is an original and together form one instrument.
8.9 This Agreement and any dispute or claim arising out of or in connection with it or its subject matter or formation (including non-contractual disputes or claims) shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the law of England and Wales.
8.10 Each Party irrevocably agrees that the courts of England and Wales shall have exclusive jurisdiction to settle any dispute or claim arising out of or in connection with this Agreement or its subject matter or formation.
